column2: As a runner, I want to record my runs so that I can track my training consistently.
column3: ['I stay active by running regularly and keeping track of my training so I can prepare properly for my next marathon.']

column2: As a runner, I want to view mileage, pace, and run frequency so that I can measure my progress toward a marathon.
column3: ['I track mileage, pace, and how I feel afterward.', 'I look at mileage, pace, and how consistent I’ve been week to week.']

column2: As a runner, I want to monitor heart rate and heart-rate recovery during and after runs so that I can assess training effort and recovery.
column3: ['I also pay attention to my heart rate, recovery time, and how I feel during and after each run.']

column3: ['I track mileage, pace, and how I feel afterward.', 'I also pay attention to my heart rate, recovery time, and how I feel during and after each run, since pace alone doesn’t tell the whole story.']

As a runner, I want workout data from my wearable to be sent to the server for remote processing so that performance and recovery metrics can be calculated.
As a runner, I want to monitor my weekly training consistency so that I can ensure I am progressing gradually without increasing mileage too quickly.
column3: ['I’m working toward it gradually and trying to stay consistent.', 'I usually run four days a week... but I’m careful not to increase distance too quickly.', 'I look at mileage, pace, and how consistent I’ve been week to week.']

column2: As a runner, I want to track weekday and weekend runs separately so that I can monitor short runs, long runs, and marathon preparation.
column3: ['I usually run four days a week, with one longer run on the weekend and shorter, easier runs during the week.', 'My weekday runs are usually around 3 to 5 miles, while the weekend long run starts closer to 8 or 10 miles and gradually increases.']

column2: As a runner, I want to record cross-training activities such as cycling, elliptical workouts, walking, strength training, stretching, and yoga so that I can maintain a balanced training plan.
column3: ['I also make sure to take rest or cross-training days so I don’t overdo it.', 'I’ll cycle or use the elliptical for lower-impact cardio, and I do strength training... I also include some stretching or yoga for mobility. On easier days, I might just take a walk.']

column2: As a runner, I want to log strength-training sessions, exercises, sets, and equipment used so that I can track supporting workouts without compromising my running.
column3: ['I usually do strength work twice a week, using moderate-weight dumbbells and resistance bands.', 'I focus on functional, unilateral movements—things like split squats, step-ups, deadlifts, rows, and presses—along with core stabilization exercises such as planks and dead bugs.', 'I keep the load controlled... usually two or three sets with enough recovery that it doesn’t compromise my running.']

column2: As a runner, I want to monitor sleep quality, hydration, nutrition, and recurring aches so that I can understand factors affecting my training and recovery.
column3: ['I also monitor my sleep, hydration, nutrition, and whether I’m having any recurring aches.']

column2: As a runner, I want to plan and save running routes so that I can compare performance on consistent routes and vary longer runs when needed.
column3: ['I also check the weather, plan routes with water access, and use cross-training to keep from overloading the same muscles.', 'I keep my weekday routes fairly consistent so I can compare my pace and effort, but I change up the longer weekend route every couple of weeks.']

column2: As a runner, I want to identify water fountains and refill locations along routes so that I can stay hydrated during longer runs.
column3: ['I usually look for public fountains or places where I can stop briefly and top off my bottle during the run.']

column2: As a runner, I want to record planned bottle-drop locations for a route so that I can prepare for workouts without reliable water access.
column3: ['I’ll also sometimes leave a bottle along the route ahead of time if it’s a particularly long workout.']

column2: As a runner, I want to check weather conditions when planning a workout so that I can adjust my route or training appropriately.
column3: ['I’m... checking the weather before I head out.', 'I’ll adjust it for different terrain, weather, or water access.']

column2: As a runner, I want a fatigue view that combines sleep quality, resting heart rate, heart-rate recovery, soreness, perceived effort, and pace so that I can assess my overall training readiness.
column3: ['I’d want a simple fatigue view that combines sleep quality, resting heart rate, heart-rate recovery, soreness, and how hard the run felt compared with the pace.']

column2: As a runner, I want to see fatigue indicators as a trend over multiple days so that I am not forced to change my plan because of a single poor result.
column3: ['Ideally it would show a trend rather than just a single score, because one poor night shouldn’t automatically change my plan.']

column2: As a runner, I want to enter a quick morning rating for energy and soreness on a one-to-five scale so that my subjective condition is included in fatigue assessment.
column3: ['I’d also like to add a quick morning rating—say, energy and soreness on a one-to-five scale—because the numbers don’t always capture how I actually feel.']

column2: As a runner, I want the app to identify worsening fatigue indicators over several days so that I can recognize possible overreaching or injury risk early.
column3: ['If several indicators worsen for a few days, I’d use that as a signal...', 'I watch cumulative training stress, sleep quality, heart-rate recovery, and soreness so I can adjust intensity before I get into overreaching or risk an injury.']

column2: As a runner, I want fatigue insights to help me decide whether to shorten a run, slow the pace, or substitute cycling or mobility work so that I can adjust training safely.
column3: ['If several indicators worsen for a few days, I’d use that as a signal to shorten a run, slow the pace, or substitute cycling or mobility work.']
